parsed.summary: The formal statements define R_k(3) as the least n such that every k-colouring of the edges of K_n has a monochromatic triangle. They then assert four things: (i) R_k(3)^{1/k} → ∞; (ii) for every k ≥ 2, R_k(3) ≥ (k^{1/3}/(6e^{38} log k))^k, together with (i); (iii) for every ε > 0 and all large k, (1/3−ε) k log k ≤ log R_k(3) ≤ (1+ε) k log k; (iv) log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k). The definitions match the standard notion, and the statements match or strengthen Theorem 1.1. The only notable caveat is that Lean fixes the explicit constant c = 1/(6e^{38}) where the paper only asserts some c > 0 (Lean is stronger); the Shannon-capacity reformulation is not formalized.

glossary.plain: A k-colouring C of the edges of K_n (vertex set Fin n) such that no colour class contains a triangle (K_3).
Every k-colouring of E(K_n) contains a monochromatic triangle.
R_k(3): the least n such that every k-colouring of E(K_n) has a monochromatic triangle.
glossary.note: By Ramsey's theorem the set is nonempty for every k, so sInf is the true minimum. Degenerate small cases (e.g. k=0 gives 2, since no 0-colouring of K_2 exists) are irrelevant to the asymptotic statements.

lean_claims.plain: For all integers k ≥ 2, ((1/(6e^{38})) · k^{1/3} / log k)^k ≤ R_k(3); and R_k(3)^{1/k} → +∞.
For every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large k: (1/3−ε) k log k ≤ log R_k(3) ≤ (1+ε) k log k.
log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k) as k → ∞.

paper_claims.plain: There is an absolute constant c > 0 such that R_k(3) ≥ (c k^{1/3}/log k)^k for every integer k ≥ 2.
The Shannon capacity of graphs with independence number 2 is unbounded.

coverage.why: Lean names the specific constant c = 1/(6e^{38}) instead of asserting that some c exists.
The ε-eventually form is exactly the o(1) exponents on both sides.
log R_k = Θ(k log k) is equivalent to R_k = k^{Θ(k)}.
No statement about Shannon capacity appears in the Lean file.

flags.explanation: Lean fixes c = 1/(6e^{38}), whereas the excerpt only claims that some absolute c > 0 exists. This makes Lean stronger than the excerpt; whether the paper body uses this specific constant is not in the excerpt.
The Shannon-capacity consequence is not formalized. The explicit factorial upper bound (2) is also only reflected through its asymptotic consequence.
